outcome_detail.summary:
I have drafted a complete transfer pricing Master File for the Freshworks Group for FY2023, following the Legora Master File template structure section by section (title page/document control, glossary, introduction, group profile, business model and value chain, IP/DEMPE, TP policy framework, treasury and capital structure, financial performance, tax compliance, plus appendices).

**Structure delivered (60 sections):** Sections 1–9 and Appendices A–C follow the template headings exactly (including 4.3.1 Procurement and Inbound Logistics through 4.3.4 After-Sales and Support, 5.2.1–5.2.4 DEMPE, 6.1–6.6 policy framework, 7.1–7.5 treasury, 8.1–8.2 financial performance, 9.1–9.3 tax compliance). I added one supplementary section — Section 10, "Open Items and Recommended Actions" — which is cross-referenced from the substantive sections and explains the qualifications attaching to the file.

**Substantive content:** grounded in the matter documents — the FY2021–FY2023 intercompany ledger (US$319.2m of recorded service fees in FY2023, by entity and year, with a three-year reconciliation of US$905.7m), the audited statutory accounts of each subsidiary, the FY2023 Form 10-K (revenue US$596.4m, operating loss US$170.2m, SBC US$210.7m, single operating segment, revenue by geography), the IP register, the functional analysis interview record, and the eleven benchmark studies (IQRs, medians, tested parties).

**Key analytical findings flagged:** (i) the 15.00% mark-up paid to Freshworks Technologies Private Limited lies outside the Group's own Asia-Pacific benchmark range of 8.34%–10.37%, implying a recurring annual adjustment of US$10.4–12.8m and a ~US$30–40m three-year exposure; (ii) Natero Ireland's 5.00% mark-up is below its range's lower bound (8.58%); (iii) the methodology tab's 12–18% contract-R&D range is unsupported by any study; (iv) management's descriptions of royalties and management fees correspond to no recorded transaction, agreement or benchmark; (v) management's description of intercompany loans is contradicted by the loan register; (vi) the contracting-party/distributor/service-provider characterisation is internally inconsistent; (vii) FW-AU and FW-SG are absent from the ledger and no accounts exist; (viii) no executed intercompany agreement was supplied (Appendix B records all as "Not provided").

Financial figures were verified against the primary filings and the entity accounts; where data could not be extracted (e.g. some FY2022 items, FW-AU/SG accounts) this is stated rather than estimated.
